:::{#thm-orthogonal-norm}
#### Orthogonal matrices preserve length

If $\matr{Q}$ is a $p \times p$ orthogonal matrix (@def-orthogonal-matrix)
and $\vx$ is a vector of length $p$, then

$$
\norm{\matr{Q}\vx} = \norm{\vx}
$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\norm{\matr{Q}\vx}^2
&= (\matr{Q}\vx) \cdot (\matr{Q}\vx)
&& \text{(definition of the Euclidean norm)}
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{Q}\vx)}\,(\matr{Q}\vx)
&& \text{(dot product as a matrix product)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\,\tp{\matr{Q}}\,(\matr{Q}\vx)
&& \text{(transpose of a product)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\,(\tp{\matr{Q}}\matr{Q})\,\vx
&& \text{(regroup; matrix multiplication is associative)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\,\matr{I}_p\,\vx
&& \text{(definition of an orthogonal matrix)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\,\vx
&& \text{(identity matrix)}
\\
&= \norm{\vx}^2
&& \text{(definition of the Euclidean norm)}
\ea
$$

Both norms are nonnegative square roots,
so equal squares give $\norm{\matr{Q}\vx} = \norm{\vx}$.
The second step is @exm-dot-product-matmul,
the third is @thm-transpose-product,
and the fourth is @thm-matmul-assoc.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-orthogonal-norm}
#### Rotating a vector keeps its length

With $\matr{Q}$ from @exm-orthogonal-matrix
and $\vx = (3, 4)$ from @exm-euclidean-norm:

$$
\ba
\matr{Q}\vx
&= \begin{bmatrix} 0.6 \cd 3 - 0.8 \cd 4 \\ 0.8 \cd 3 + 0.6 \cd 4 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of matrix-vector multiplication)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} -1.4 \\ 4.8 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

$$
\ba
\norm{\matr{Q}\vx}
&= \sqrt{(-1.4)^2 + 4.8^2}
&& \text{(definition of the norm)}
\\
&= \sqrt{1.96 + 23.04}
&& \text{(square)}
\\
&= \sqrt{25}
&& \text{(add)}
\\
&= 5
\ea
$$

which is $\norm{\vx} = 5$.

:::
